column1: Pour boiling water over the spinach in a colander and let it cool. Squeeze out as much water as possible by hand and then in a clean towel, and chop finely.
Mix the spinach with the ricotta, Parmesan, garlic, lemon zest, and nutmeg. Season well and load into a piping bag with a 1–2cm nozzle.
Lay out the ready-rolled fresh pasta sheets, reserving half to cover the filling. Allow enough space to cut out four 10cm ravioli.
Pipe four 7cm rings of filling on the bottom sheets, leaving enough room around each for cutting and sealing, then pipe a second layer on top to form 2cm-high walls.
Gently drop an egg yolk into the middle of each ring.
Brush the pasta around the filling with water, lay the reserved sheets over the top, and press around each mound to push out any air.
Cut out the ravioli with a 10cm round cutter and pinch the edges to seal well.
Lower the ravioli into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook for 3 minutes, then lift into two serving bowls.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the sage for 1–2 minutes until crisp.
Spoon the sage butter over the ravioli, top with extra Parmesan if you like, and serve at once.
